note: Every entry below was opened by this session on 2026-11-12 (UTC) and the quoted text was read on the publisher's own page. A page that could not be opened is recorded with status 'blocked' and an empty claim, and is published on flagged.html.

sources.claim: Practice Report: injured players are listed as Did Not Participate, Limited Participation ('less than 100 percent of a player's normal repetitions') or Full Participation ('100 percent of a player's normal repetitions'). Game Status Report: 'Questionable means it is uncertain as to whether the player will play in the game; Doubtful means it is unlikely the player will participate; and Out means the player will not play.' The 'Probable' category was eliminated 'because approximately 95 percent of the players who were listed as "Probable" in prior years did in fact play in the game.' A player certain to play is not listed on the Game Status Report; if he is then deactivated 'the club will be required to provide an explanation to the league, and will be subject to possible discipline.'
sources.supports: The only official definitions of the practice and game-status fields; the basis for every injury signal in this project.
sources.method: Opened the NFL.com article and read the full body text.

sources.claim: Page title: 'Official Latest NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season'. The page is a per-game, per-club table with the columns Player, Position, Injuries, Practice Status, Game Status. At the time of reading (2026-11-12) the Practice Status column was populated for every listed player and the Game Status column was populated for only a minority of players.
sources.supports: The live official injury feed. This project had no injury data before this session; this page is the only official event-level source used.
sources.method: Opened the page and read all 7 rendered chunks; 244 player rows transcribed to decisions/data/injuries_week10_2026.json.

sources.supports: No official public participation/snap-count page exists at this URL (404 'Page Not Found'). Snap counts and participation are therefore NOT an official public dataset, which is why the role-depth model here is defined from the published depth ordering plus market repricing, not from snap counts.
sources.method: Requested the URL; 404.

sources.claim: 'A "Same Game Parlay" is a Parlay with each leg being from the same Event.' 'If leg(s) of a Same Game Parlay are voided or settled as Push, the entire stake amount will not be returned and instead will remain on the Parlay with the remaining number of legs.' A Push does not protect the bettor: the parlay is repriced on the remaining legs, at the odds available when the SGP was placed.
sources.supports: The operator's own rule: the house re-prices same-game combinations. Any correlation the bettor can measure is only worth something after this repricing, which is the central constraint on every parlay strategy in this project.
sources.method: Opened the Market Rules page and read the Same Game Parlay section.

sources.claim: 'A "Parlay" is a bet with two or more legs and requires every leg to be settled as won in order for the Parlay to be settled as won.' Voided/pushed legs reduce the parlay and the odds are recalculated on the remaining legs.
sources.supports: Definition of the multi-leg product the project is trying to price.
sources.method: Read the Parlay section of the same page.

sources.claim: 'Generally, if a player starts or meets the playing time requirements as described in the House Rules, then all bets will stand and be settled accordingly.' For players who do not start, the article directs the reader to the sport-specific House Rules.
sources.supports: Player props depend on a playing-time threshold that differs by book and by market. A player who is active but on a snap count can still lose a prop whose underlying number he would have cleared at full usage.
sources.method: Opened the article and read the body.

sources.claim: 'If a whole number is offered as the point spread or handicap, bets will be settled as Push if the outcome bet on is tied after the point spread or handicap for the bet has been applied.'
sources.supports: Why push handling must be explicit in every ROI calculation (the project's own bets table reports pushes).
sources.method: Read the 2-Way Point Spread Markets section.

sources.claim: 'Doing pairwise comparison procedures over and over again for all possible pairs will not, in general, work. This is because the overall significance level is not as specified for a single pair comparison.' Also: 'If the decision on what comparisons to make is withheld until after the data are examined' then a multiple-comparison procedure is required.
sources.supports: The statistical rule that makes an 18-rule search over one dataset inadmissible without multiplicity control: the reason the project's own 18 rules pass 0 of 8 gates, and the reason a leaderboard must pre-register.
sources.method: Opened the NIST page and read section 7.4.7.

sources.claim: Root mean square error: 'The RMSE is the square root of the average of the squares of the errors' — i.e. RMSE is an average of squared error, not an average absolute error.
sources.supports: Why 'own-line error 10.670 pts' must be labelled MAE, not RMSE: recomputing RMSE on the same predictions gives 13.618 (decision section D05).
sources.method: Opened the NIST RMSE page.
